newsitem.title: INDIA: India criticised over Kashmir activist probe.
newsitem.headline: India criticised over Kashmir activist probe.

text.p: Amnesty International has accused the Indian government of failing to cooperate with an investigation into last year's death of a leading human rights activist in Kashmir.
The body of prominent lawyer and human rights activist Jalil Andrabi was discovered on March 27, 1996, in the Jhelum River in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
The chairman of the Kashmir Commission of Jurists, Andrabi had been abducted two weeks earlier by unidentified gunmen as he was driving home with his family.
His wife said Indian security forces had picked him up, but the army denied the charge.
Andrabi's killing sparked international condemnation and calls for a full investigation.

"Despite a special investigation under the direction of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court, the truth has still not been revealed," London-based Amnesty International said in a statement released on Thursday in New Delhi.
"The Indian government seems content to consign his fate, like hundreds of other human rights victims, to oblivion," the human rights group said.
Indian government officials hotly denied this claim.

"The special investigating team of the police has already submitted its report to the High Court about the Jalil Andrabi case, so from our side there is no delay", Jammu and Kashmir state government spokesman K.B. Jandial told Reuters.
Officials said the investigation team had told the Srinagar bench of the state high court on April 10 that a major in the territorial army was reponsible for the killing.
Police and hospital officials say that more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence since a separatist revolt began in Jammu and Kashmir in 1990.

Amnesty said the names of suspects in the Andrabi case had not been made public and no one had been arrested or suspended. By mid-March 1997, no post mortem report had been submitted to the investigating team.
It said the Indian government had responded to a September 1996 report by Amnesty International on the killings of Andrabi and another activist.
"The allegations of government hand in the killing of human rights activists in Jammu and Kashmir have been made earlier also," Amnesty quoted the government response as saying.

"In all incidents of killings of so-called human rights activists, government has made available clinching evidence showing that they were targets of one or other militant organisation, whose ideology did not match theirs," it said.

Amnesty said the government response was not "meaningful" and called on the state government to ensure the speedy conclusion of the investigation and the suspension or indictment of those involved in the murder.
It also called on the state government to publicly commit itself "to ending impunity".
